title: Capturing Values in Closures
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of capturing values in closures in a Swift program or workflow.
Apply captured variables and constants in a small, inspectable example.
Check the expected result and identify one boundary case or platform constraint.

content.intro: This lesson focuses on capturing values in closures and the practical choices around it. Start with the smallest example, connect it to “Captured variables and constants”, and verify the result before adding complexity.
content.why_it_matters: Reusable functions and precise data models reduce duplication. Handling missing data and failures explicitly makes later application code safer to change.

content_blocks.text: **Start with the rule.** `let` binds a value that cannot be reassigned. Prefer it unless the program genuinely needs to change the binding.

**Work through the lesson.** Turn repeated behavior into clear functions, then use closures when behavior itself needs to be passed around. The detailed subtopic list in this lesson preserves the curriculum coverage; treat each item as a cue for a small example or a focused question rather than trying to memorize syntax.

items.title: Captured variables and constants
items.text: `let` binds a value that cannot be reassigned. Prefer it unless the program genuinely needs to change the binding.

items.title: Capture lists
items.text: A closure packages behavior that can be passed or stored. Check which values it captures and whether it can outlive the current call before choosing capture semantics.
